name: infra_sagemaker_entry
title: SageMaker script mode: a training entrypoint and four inference hooks with no call site, in one module
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-infra: the file that is a trainer and a server at the same time
note: One planted defect (MLV803 at line 143), recovered at 0.950. The precision claim is the other half: `predict_fn` runs the model, computes a softmax and returns it, and `model_fn` loads a state dict - and neither is drawn as a training loop or reported as an unguarded evaluation, because both call model.eval() and predict_fn carries @torch.no_grad(). The configuration arrives entirely through os.environ defaults on argparse arguments, which MLView resolves into the config lane (21 nodes). One observation, not a finding: `workspace.frameworks` reports `pandas` on a file with no pandas import, because `features.astype("float32")` at line 69 on a numpy array resolves to `pandas.DataFrame.astype` - see INFRA-R2-06.
stagesObserved: config, data, model, objective, train, eval and deliver present; preprocess absent, which is correct - nothing here transforms features. local and ip are byte-identical.

expected.defect: model_fn calls torch.load with neither weights_only= nor map_location=
expected.why: the SageMaker training instance has a GPU and the inference instance usually does not, so this load raises on the endpoint; and it unpickles arbitrary objects out of an artefact bucket

forbidden.why: the training loader is built with shuffle=True at line 112
the validation loader is built with shuffle=False at line 113
no DataLoader here passes num_workers, and the module ends in an `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is at line 80, before the forward at 81
optimizer.step() is called at line 84, after loss.backward() at line 83
the order is zero_grad (80) -> forward (81) -> loss (82) -> backward (83) -> step (84)
the epoch loss is accumulated as running += loss.item(), a Python float
CosineAnnealingLR is epoch-cadence and scheduler.step() is called in the epoch loop at line 128
validate() calls model.eval() at line 92, model_fn calls it at line 145 and predict_fn calls it at line 158; every path that runs the model outside training switches mode first
validate() carries @torch.no_grad() at line 89 and predict_fn carries it at line 156
the accuracy comparison at line 98 is on model(features).argmax(dim=1), not on raw logits
FraudNet.forward returns raw logits and nn.CrossEntropyLoss is fed exactly that; the torch.softmax at line 160 is in predict_fn, on the serving path, and never reaches a loss
there is no BCELoss and no BCEWithLogitsLoss in this file

the model is moved at line 115 and both loops move every batch value to the same device before the forward (78-79 and 96-97); predict_fn runs on whatever device the endpoint loaded the model onto and has no loop
the device is chosen behind torch.cuda.is_available() at line 107; there is no unguarded .cuda()
seed_everything(args.seed) at line 106 calls random.seed, numpy.random.seed, torch.manual_seed and torch.cuda.manual_seed_all
there is no sklearn splitter and no random_split; SageMaker mounts train and validation as two separate input channels
FraudNet.__init__ calls super().__init__() as its first statement at line 42
the body is an nn.Sequential; there is no plain list or dict of submodules

unsupported.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2: MLV903 is not a built rule - it carries the status **later** in docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 1 - so a label for it can never be satisfied and can never be violated. `analyzer/tests/accuracy/test_accuracy.py::test_every_labelled_code_is_a_real_rule` rejects one, and this row turned that shipped test red. The observation is kept verbatim here so the row can be restored the day the rule ships. Original verdict `forbidden`, original note: model_fn, input_fn, predict_fn and output_fn have no call site by design - SageMaker calls them by name - so an orphan-stage claim about them would be wrong
